A different job from a floor plan

One explains the tenancy. The other explains the site.

A commercial floor plan shows how internal spaces connect. Measured site and boundary mapping works at the property or land level: where the subject sits, how large the holding is, where its boundaries run, what the frontage looks like and how it relates to roads, stations, retail, ports, ring roads or the CBD.

For many industrial, logistics, land and development campaigns, both layers can be useful in the same brief.

What can be mapped

Information that belongs on the image, not buried in a paragraph.

Site area & dimensions

Published or briefed site area, key boundary dimensions and parcel scale can be placed directly onto the aerial frame.

Boundary & frontage

Subject-site outlines and frontage can make land, development and industrial holdings easier to identify at a glance.

Access & circulation

Road approach, hardstand, loading areas and relevant access points can be highlighted when they are part of the marketing brief.

Transport & amenity

Stations, ring roads, ports, airport, CBD, retail centres and other relevant context can be positioned around the subject site.

Land & development

Large parcels and development sites can be shown with dimensions and surrounding context without asking an enquiry to interpret a raw aerial alone.

Industrial & logistics

Warehouses, estates and logistics assets can combine site identification with access, surrounding infrastructure and operational context.

Where it fits

Part of a commercial media brief, not a disconnected add-on.

Measured mapping can be scoped alongside commercial property photography, CASA-certified aerial, film and commercial floor plans. Keeping those outputs in one visual system helps the agency present the asset consistently across portals, brochures, information memorandums and direct enquiry follow-up.

24-hour delivery is available for commercial photography. Mapping, measurement, video and larger briefs are scoped against the campaign deadline.

Direct answers

Measured site-plan questions.

Is this a legal survey?

No. These are marketing plans and property-media overlays unless a separate professional or statutory scope is expressly agreed. Survey, title, planning, architectural or legal decisions should rely on the appropriate qualified documentation.

Can boundaries and dimensions be shown on drone photography?

Yes. Where the brief provides or confirms the relevant information, site outlines, dimensions, area, frontage and contextual labels can be integrated into aerial property imagery.

Can site mapping be booked with photography and floor plans?

Yes. Sixth Vision Commercial can combine still photography, CASA-certified aerial, film, measured floor plans and site or amenity mapping in one commercial campaign brief.
